definitions.explanation: Suffix indicating a style, form, or manner of doing something.

examples.japanese: {筆記|ひっき}{体|たい}で{書|か}く。
{活字|かつじ}{体|たい}と{手書|てが}き{体|たい}は{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: Printed font and handwritten style are different.

examples.japanese: {敬|けい}{体|たい}と{常|じょう}{体|たい}を{使|つか}い{分|わ}ける。
examples.english: Use polite and plain styles appropriately.

notes:
{体|たい} is a suffix indicating a style, form, or manner.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:

Writing/Font styles:
- {筆記|ひっき}{体|たい}: cursive script
- {活字|かつじ}{体|たい}: printed font
- {明朝|みんちょう}{体|たい}: Ming/Mincho typeface
- ゴシック{体|たい}: Gothic typeface

Grammatical styles:
- {敬|けい}{体|たい}: polite form (です/ます)
- {常|じょう}{体|たい}: plain form (dictionary form)

Other uses:
- {液|えき}{体|たい}: liquid (state of matter)
- {固|こ}{体|たい}: solid
- {気|き}{体|たい}: gas

USAGE:
{体|たい} as a suffix differs from {体|からだ} (body). When attached to other kanji, it typically indicates a style, form, or state.
